prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM System. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (own authority). Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System: Regional Flow Platform alias Cedarbell (coordination only; shall expose regional demand/constraint context to shared workspace each publication cycle, no manual re-entry). Parts: Demand Prediction Service alias Marlinstone, Capacity Assessment Module (CAM), Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal alias Foxglove, Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway alias Orchard, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log (who/when/provisional-or-confirmed/dependent decision; disputes), runway meters, apron sensors, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display (marks service-supplied, user-confirmed, stale values). Actors: Regional Flow Manager alias Copperfin (authorizes measures); Airline Operations Coordinator alias Saffron (Flight Intent Message, Target Off Block Time); Slot Coordinator (Calculated Takeoff Time feasibility; logs slot adjustments/conflicts); Airport Duty Manager (Airport Capacity Plan; confirms mode transitions); Tower Supervisor (runway configuration, sequence feasibility before metering); Ramp Control Lead (stand release, tugs, pushback); Ground Handling Dispatcher (servicing, baggage, staffing, equipment milestones); Meteorology Briefing Officer (weather interpretation, Storm Cell Snapshot); Data Governance Steward (fields, retention, quality thresholds); System Support Engineer (availability, latency, sync); others. Flows: Flight Intent Message→Airline Interface Adapter (Business Rules Registry)→Flight Data Exchange→Marlinstone; Orchard→CAM. Requirements: participants update material change within 2 min (Normal), 1 min (Adverse Weather/Capacity Reduction); provisional value with uncertainty flag if unknown; stale milestone→Foxglove highlights flight, notifies accountable role via Alert Distribution Hub; Contingency Fallback: preserve last synchronized milestones, mark degraded updates; Recovery: frequent updates; time-stamped→Audit Event Ledger.

New part:
S173: After operations, the Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded milestones and decision history to compare planned outcomes with actual off-block, takeoff, landing, and stand events.
S174: Tower and airport duty coordination establishes the working link between live control positions, the airport duty desk, surface surveillance feeds, and operational safety checks.
S175: The Tower Supervisor remains accountable for control tower coordination and keeps the Airport Duty Manager informed of conditions that may affect runway, taxiway, stand, or apron availability.
S176: For this section only, Brindle is the operational alias used by Tower Supervisor during voice coordination drills.
S177: The Airport Duty Manager maintains the airport duty desk as the single operational point for airport status confirmation during Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase.
S178: The duty desk reviews tower inputs, airport operations reports, and surveillance indications before confirming whether a local condition should be reflected in the Airport Capacity Plan.
S179: The Surface Surveillance Adapter consolidates position updates from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor and presents movement indications to the Airport CDM Portal.
S180: The Tower Sequence Manager uses validated surface status to support local sequencing decisions without replacing controller judgment or established radio procedures.
S181: The Airport Duty Manager uses the Runway Inspection Note to confirm that the duty desk has a current record of pavement status before endorsing any declared capacity change.
S182: Orchard shall issue time-stamped weather condition updates for use in tower and airport duty coordination.
S183: When surveillance data conflicts with tower observations, the Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager agree on the operational interpretation before the condition is shared more widely.
S184: The Ramp Control Lead reviews apron movement constraints with the duty desk when stand access, pushback flow, or tug routing affects the departure plan.
S185: The Airport CDM Portal records duty desk confirmations as operational annotations linked to the relevant runway, taxiway, apron, or stand area.
S186: The Collaborative Decision Log captures the time, origin, and rationale for each local coordination decision that affects capacity or surface flow.
S187: The Time Synchronization Service shall keep tower, duty desk, surveillance, and portal event times aligned so that later review can reconstruct the sequence of events.
S188: Surface surveillance feeds are treated as advisory evidence for airport duty decisions unless the competent controller or airport authority confirms the operational effect.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
